passages.text: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon: David wrote this psalm.\r\nDavid gave this psalm to the choirmaster.\r\nThe choirmaster should use stringed instruments to perform this psalm.

passages.text: Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have relieved my distress; show me grace and hear my prayer.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He wanted it played with stringed instruments.
David speaks to God.
He calls God the God of his righteousness.
David asks God to answer him when he calls.
David says God has relieved his distress.
David asks God to show him grace.
David asks God to hear his prayer.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ בִּנְגִינ֗וֹת מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ בְּקָרְאִ֡י עֲנֵ֤נִי׀ אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י צִדְקִ֗י בַּ֭צָּר הִרְחַ֣בְתָּ לִּ֑י חָ֝נֵּ֗נִי וּשְׁמַ֥ע תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃

passages.text: How long, O men, will my honor be maligned? How long will you love vanity and seek after lies ? Selah Know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David spoke to men who opposed him.
He asked them a question.
He said, “How long will you turn my honor into shame?”
He said, “How long will you love what is worthless?”
He said, “How long will you seek after lies?”
Pause and think about this.
Know this truth.
The LORD sets apart the godly for Himself.
The LORD listens when I call to Him.
passages.original: בְּנֵ֥י אִ֡ישׁ עַד־ מֶ֬ה כְבוֹדִ֣י לִ֭כְלִמָּה תֶּאֱהָב֣וּן רִ֑יק תְּבַקְשׁ֖וּ כָזָ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃ וּדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־ הִפְלָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה חָסִ֣יד ל֑וֹ יְהוָ֥ה יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע בְּקָרְאִ֥י אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Be angry, yet do not sin; on your bed, search your heart and be still. Selah Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David speaks to the people.
He says, “Be angry, but do not sin.”
When you lie on your bed, search your heart.
Be still and quiet.
Offer right sacrifices to God.
Trust in the LORD.
passages.original: רִגְז֗וּ וְֽאַל־ תֶּ֫חֱטָ֥אוּ אִמְר֣וּ בִ֭לְבַבְכֶם עַֽל־ מִשְׁכַּבְכֶ֗ם וְדֹ֣מּוּ סֶֽלָה׃ זִבְח֥וּ זִבְחֵי־ צֶ֑דֶק וּ֝בִטְח֗וּ אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Many ask, “Who can show us the good?” Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD.
passages.sermon:
Many people speak.
They ask, “Who will show us what is good?”
LORD, let Your face shine on us.
Show us Your favor.
passages.original: רַבִּ֥ים אֹמְרִים֮ מִֽי־ יַרְאֵ֪נ֫וּ ט֥וֹב נְֽסָה־ עָ֭לֵינוּ א֨וֹר פָּנֶ֬יךָ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David says, “You have given me joy.”
This joy fills my heart.
This joy is greater than the joy people feel at harvest.
This joy is greater than the joy when grain and new wine are plentiful.
passages.original: נָתַ֣תָּה שִׂמְחָ֣ה בְלִבִּ֑י מֵעֵ֬ת דְּגָנָ֖ם וְתִֽירוֹשָׁ֣ם רָֽבּוּ׃

passages.text: I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David trusted the LORD.
David said, “I will lie down in peace.”
David said, “I will sleep.”
The LORD alone keeps me safe.
The LORD makes me live in safety.
passages.original: בְּשָׁל֣וֹם יַחְדָּו֮ אֶשְׁכְּבָ֪ה וְאִ֫ישָׁ֥ן כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה לְבָדָ֑ד לָ֝בֶ֗טַח תּוֹשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃
